target.title: fix(web-search): align credential presence with usable providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

The earlier detector could treat credentials from blocked plugins or unrelated providers as web-search credentials. The latest fix also handles the Google plugin's split contracts: selecting `gemini` no longer counts `google-vertex` env such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` as a Gemini web-search key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Security/audit surfaces should reflect the selected web-search provider's actual runtime credential contract. Plugin manifests can contain multiple providers and env vars, so manifest env scanning must not flatten unrelated provider credentials into one web-search-positive result.

## User Impact

- Disabled, denied, or non-selected web-search plugins no longer make `web_search` look credentialed.
- Missing env-backed SecretRefs fail closed consistently.
- `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` no longer reports Gemini web search as configured.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` still reports Gemini web search as configured through the selected provider contract.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 26 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine opencode` reported no accepted/actionable findings after the optional-chain cleanup.

## Proof

- Added regression coverage for Google/Gemini-vs-Vertex manifest env scoping: `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` alone is false for selected `gemini`, while `GEMINI_API_KEY` is true.
- Provider-scoped manifest env detection now first reads the selected bundled web-search provider's public contract env vars, then falls back only to same-provider manifest setup/auth env metadata when a public contract is unavailable.
- Existing policy/credential tests still cover plugin allow/deny, disabled entries, keyless providers, raw plugin webSearch credentials, SecretRefs, and explicit provider selection.



### Follow-up Evidence - 2026-07-11

- Commit `cbd771ef20` rejects explicitly configured unknown web-search providers before top-level or nested credentials can satisfy the credential-presence audit.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 26 tests.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/web-search/runtime.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 30 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.ts src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Default Codex autoreview was attempted but blocked by the local invalid OpenAI API key (401); OpenCode autoreview on the same local patch returned clean with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(firecrawl,brave,web-search,web-fetch,models-config): use own-property checks for config field lookups
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

All runtime config lookup paths use `"<key>" in <configObj>` to check whether a config field is present. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so an inherited property (e.g. via `Object.create({provider: "malicious"})`) could be mistaken for an explicit user config entry and override the normal env/default path.

### Why This Change Was Made

Use `Object.hasOwn()` which only checks own properties — inherited prototype properties are ignored. Config objects are plain POJOs from JSON, so `Object.hasOwn()` behaves identically for all legitimate config shapes while closing the prototype-chain attack surface.

### User Impact

No user-visible change for normal config. Prototype-chain inherited properties are no longer treated as user config entries across all runtime config lookup paths.

### Evidence

Exact head: `5a5e269d3ea`

**Validation:**

- **Focused tests** — all changed and new test files pass:
```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  6 passed (6)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/models-config.merge.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  19 passed (19)
  (includes 6 new own-property + 1 restored baseUrl regression test)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  32 passed (32)
  (includes 2 new own-property tests)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/web-fetch/runtime.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  20 passed (20)
  (includes 2 new own-property tests)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests  44 passed (44)

All together: 5 test files, 121 tests, all passed ✅
```

- **Format:** `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1` 12 changed files → all correct format ✅
- **Whitespace:** `git diff --check` → clean ✅
- **Types:** `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` → passed ✅

**Live runtime proof — Object.hasOwn() behavior on each changed path:**

```text
=== Firecrawl config.ts: Object.hasOwn(searchRecord, 'firecrawl') ===
  'firecrawl' in searchRecordWithProto: true
  Object.hasOwn(searchRecordWithProto, 'firecrawl'): false     ← inherited rejected
  Object.hasOwn(searchRecordWithProto, 'ownKey'): true         ← own preserved

=== models-config.merge.ts: Object.hasOwn(explicitModel, 'contextWindow') ===
  'contextWindow' in modelWithProtoCtx: true
  Object.hasOwn(modelWithProtoCtx, 'contextWindow'): false     ← inherited rejected
  Object.hasOwn(modelWithProtoCtx, 'ownCtx'): true             ← own preserved

=== web-search/runtime.ts: Object.hasOwn(search, 'provider') ===
  'provider' in searchWithProtoProvider: true
  Object.hasOwn(searchWithProtoProvider, 'provider'): false    ← inherited rejected
  Object.hasOwn(searchWithProtoProvider, 'ownProvider'): true  ← own preserved

=== web-fetch/runtime.ts: Object.hasOwn(fetch, 'provider') ===
  'provider' in fetchWithProtoProvider: true
  Object.hasOwn(fetchWithProtoProvider, 'provider'): false     ← inherited rejected

=== brave/web-search-shared.ts: Object.hasOwn(search, 'apiKey') ===
  'apiKey' in searchWithProtoKey: true
  Object.hasOwn(searchWithProtoKey, 'apiKey'): false           ← inherited rejected
  Object.hasOwn(searchWithProtoKey, 'ownKey'): true            ← own preserved

RESULT: All changed paths correctly use Object.hasOwn() to reject proto-inherited fields.
```

Every test calls the real `mergeProviderModels()`, `resolveFirecrawlSearchConfig()` and similar production functions — no simulation, no stubs.

### Files Changed

| File | Changes |
|---|---|
| `extensions/firecrawl/src/config.ts` | `"firecrawl" in search/fetch` → `Object.hasOwn()` (2) |
| `extensions/brave/web-search-shared.ts` | `"apiKey" in search` → `Object.hasOwn()` (1) |
| `extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts` | New: 6 tests for own-property behavior |
| `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | `"provider" in search/params.search` → `Object.hasOwn()` (4) |
| `src/web-fetch/runtime.ts` | `"provider" in params.fetch` → `Object.hasOwn()` (2) |
| `src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts` | `maxCharsCap/maxResponseBytes/provider/userAgent` → `Object.hasOwn()` (4) |
| `src/agents/models-config.merge.ts` | `contextWindow/contextTokens/maxTokens/input/reasoning` → `Object.hasOwn()` (5) |
| `src/cli/capability-cli.ts` | `"apiKey" in value` → `Object.hasOwn()` (1) |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.ts` | `"apiKey" in search` → `Object.hasOwn()` (1) |

**Scope note:** The `test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` change in this PR is a test-tooling-only fix (restored a pre-existing `baseUrl` regression). No runtime Firecrawl config semantics changed beyond the `Object.hasOwn()` hardening.
